answer.label: In short
answer.lead: White-label web design is the design stage of a website, produced by MMC for your agency to present as its own: structure, wireframes, page layouts and a design system, all to your client's brand. You choose whether your developers build it or hand it to our development team.
answer.hl: structure, wireframes, page layouts and a design system
answer.who: Monday Marketing Company (MMC) delivers web design for agencies and works behind your brand. You own the client relationship; we do the work.

paras: Design goes wrong when it is disconnected from build. We design with development in mind: components that can be built, states that are specified and files that are named clearly.
Our direct approach is on the UI/UX design page, and build can follow through white-label web development.

stages.breaks: Starting design from a one-line brief.
stages.why: Your designer guesses the brand and the goal, and your client corrects both after the first presentation.
stages.does: We take a structured brief with brand files, goals and references from you, and write down what is in scope before the first layout.

stages.breaks: Revision rounds that nobody wrote down.
stages.why: Every extra round is unbilled work, and open-ended feedback is how a fixed fee turns into a loss.
stages.does: The scope states the rounds. Extra rounds are quoted before we start them, so you can bill your client for them.

stages.breaks: Designing past what the platform can build.
stages.why: A beautiful layout that the CMS cannot do becomes a rebuild, and the delay lands on you.
stages.does: We design with WordPress, Shopify or custom limits in mind, and flag anything costly before your client falls for it.

stages.why: Unnamed layers and missing states send your developers back with questions, and the build date slips.
stages.does: Components, states and notes are named clearly, in the format you or your build partner prefer.

stages.breaks: Feedback spread across emails and chats.
stages.why: Versions get mixed up and the last comment wins, not the right one.
stages.does: One feedback route, one version in play, and a short change list we send you after each round to forward on.
